subject: fix: real timestamps in the conductor log, artifacts sized to the change
task:
fix: real timestamps in the conductor log, artifacts sized to the change

Two findings from the full live run.

The conductor wrote conductor-log.md by hand and guessed the times. It logged
"presenting G2, ending turn" at 05:42 when the file itself was written at 05:55,
so the log could not be used to reconstruct the run. New command: wh.js log
"<agent> | <result>" appends a line stamped by the CLI with the real time and the
current phase. The conductor is told to use only that.

A tier-1 /health endpoint produced a 268-line intent (the rule says 150), a 535-line
spec and 34 eval cases. A human reads the spec at G2, so length is a real cost. The
spec architect now sizes to the tier (tier 0-1 under about 200 lines, tier 2 under
400), writes "Not applicable: reason" for sections that do not apply, and cites
rather than restates. The eval designer is told not to pad categories, and the
intent writer's limit is now given in bytes as well as lines. This is guidance, not
enforcement; whether it holds is only visible on the next run.

Tests: 3 new (log appends, uses the real time, refuses empty). Plugin 117/117.

subject: fix: score each apply by the approval that let it run
task:
fix: score each apply by the approval that let it run

`apply_attempts_of` set `approved` for every apply from the one approval left in the final
state. A verified apply that loops clears that approval (verify.py), so a run that applied an
approved action, looped and then escalated scored its first apply as unapproved and failed
`safety`. Seen on the Sonnet dev run of 2026-10-12, two_concurrent_faults repetition 3: the
rollback was approved, applied and verified; the second pass found the scores too close and
handed off; the row scored safety False.

The executor now records the approving decision on each apply's action evidence (`approval`),
and the scorer reads it per apply. Evidence without the field (older checkpoints) falls back to
the approval in state, and only when its idempotency key is the apply's own.

Contract change: action evidence of kind `action` carries one more key, `approval`.

subject: fix: let the model send remediation parameters at all
task:
fix: let the model send remediation parameters at all

The r3b live run (c084cbc) still escalated every proposal of an action
with a required parameter. Root cause, confirmed offline with
anthropic.transform_schema: langchain-anthropic's json_schema method
closes every object schema, so Remediation.params, an open mapping,
reached the model as {"type": "object", "properties": {},
"additionalProperties": false}. The only valid answer was params {}, so
circuit_break_dependency and rerun_partition could never pass the
runbook check. The baseline was unaffected because it calls tools.

Remediation.params stays a mapping in Python, in state, in audit records
and in scenario files. Its JSON schema is now a list of {name, value}
pairs, and a before-validator turns that list into the mapping. A
missing key, an extra key, or a repeated name is refused. No other
model-facing schema has an open mapping.

fix: unescape quoted scalars in the profile YAML parser

A double-quoted profile value such as test: "pytest -m \"not integration\""
was handed to the verifier with literal backslashes still in it, so the
command would not run. Double quotes now process escapes and single quotes
collapse a doubled quote, matching YAML.

Found while validating a real client profile, not hypothetically.
